text:
B: Hello! There she is. You're Gemma?
A: Hiya, yes, hello! You're Marijke. Have I said that right?
B: Perfect, better than most. You look like your picture, with the glasses.
A: Oh, well, I wear them all day, I can't see the labels without them. Your tulip picture's lovely, behind you.
B: Ah, that's home. Holland. I'm Dutch, but forty years in Kent now. So what do you do, love?
A: I'm a pharmacy technician, at the hospital in Nottingham. I check people's medicines when they come onto the ward.
B: Oh, medicines! I do the tablets with my ladies in the mornings. Well, I don't give them, I prompt. You've taken your blue one, Doris? Yes, she says, and then I find it in the cup.
A: Ha, that happens on the wards as well. Patients tell you they're taking something and they stopped it two years ago. Or they've got three boxes of the same thing under different names and they're taking all three. It's sort of my job to catch that, so I go through everything and ring the GP and the family. My dad's the same, actually, he's got heart tablets and I keep an eye on his dosette box every Sunday.
B: Good girl. Keith won't even go to the doctor. His blood pressure, I don't know. I say, Keith, go, and he says, I'm fine.
A: Oh, they're all the same. Do you want me to tell him? I'll be very stern.
B: Please. Write him a letter.
A: Ha, I will. So you're a carer?
B: Morning calls. Twelve hours a week, finished by eleven. I like it. My knees don't like it, all the stairs.
A: I bet. I couldn't do what you do, honestly, the washing and dressing. The carers we get on discharge are amazing.
B: Everyone can do it. Not everyone wants to, that's the difference.
A: That's true. Erm, do you have family near you?
B: Son in Maidstone, daughter in Rochester, three grandkids. Every weekend I'm feeding everybody. Have you got kids?
A: No. No, we haven't. Erm, I've got a niece and nephew, though, my brother's two, so I'm a very busy auntie.
B: That's the best job. You give them back.
A: Ha, that's exactly what my mum says. She was a dinner lady, actually, years ago.
B: Zain said I look like a dinner lady! I think it was nice.
A: Oh, it's a compliment from him, definitely. He was lovely about his mum.
B: Yes, very nice boy. What else, erm... what do you do at the weekend?
A: Parkrun on a Saturday, dog walk, and a bit of cross-stitch. That's mine behind me, the cottage. It's a bit wonky.
B: No, it's lovely. I can't do anything like that, I do word searches.
A: Oh, word searches are good for winding down. Oh, I think the time's nearly gone.
B: Tell Keith to go to the doctor, yes?
A: I'll send the letter.
